title: Friendly and accountable
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Can you be a friend and still hold someone to account?

Jose read another point: camaraderie is dangerous. It makes it hard for people to challenge each other's work, and there is a tendency not to want to throw colleagues under the bus. What do you think?
A student said: I have been guilty of getting too friendly in the workplace, and then it is hard to hold people accountable once you let that boundary be crossed.
Jose asked: how do you be the friendly, approachable person, so people take risks, and at the same time not tolerate mediocrity?

A student said: first, setting clear expectations. Second, not letting things slide, with accountability immediately. Once you have drawn that line, you can be friendlier. If you lead with happy-go-lucky, in my experience you get taken advantage of.

Another said: I have requirements, not expectations. The only thing I can control is my involvement in a situation. If the requirements aren't met, I subtract myself or I subtract what isn't being met. If we have known each other long enough, we should be able to respect that.

Jose said: you are talking about a specific personality that is extremely hard to find, one in a million. In a work environment it is a lot to ask for. How do you counter that with people you don't know?
A student answered: more business at first, friendly, but task-oriented. Give deadlines in a project system, and when something is past due, they hold themselves accountable.
Where is the line you draw, and do your people know it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a time friendship made accountability hard.
Write the expectations you would set on day one.
Write the requirements you hold, as distinct from expectations.
Write how you would show someone that something is overdue.
Write the line you will draw first.

check.q: What did a student say about leading with happy-go-lucky?
choices: It leads to being taken advantage of

check.q: What did one student prefer to hold instead of expectations?
What did a student say to do with deadlines?
choices: Put them in a project system so people hold themselves accountable

recap: Draw the line early. Be friendly after that. Use systems so people hold themselves accountable.
